data: GEO mobile comms — maritime, aviation, GMDSS backbone
Viasat-owned Inmarsat constellation (acquired 2023). Originally founded 1979 as International Maritime Satellite Organization, an intergovernmental treaty body.

Geostationary mobile-satellite communications — 14+ satellites in GEO providing maritime, aviation, and remote-area voice + data services. Originally founded 1979 as the International Maritime Satellite Organization, an intergovernmental treaty body for ship-to-shore comms (the predecessor of GMDSS). Privatised 1999. Acquired by Viasat in 2023 to combine with Viasat's Ka-band fleet.
Russia's GNSS — 24 sats, restored to full coverage in 2011
China's GNSS — global ops since 2020; unique MEO + IGSO + GEO hybrid
The original GNSS — 31 satellites, free public service since 2000
NOAA geostationary weather pair — Americas continuous coverage
US early-warning IR sensors hosted on classified Tundra-orbit platforms

14+ geostationary satellites providing maritime, aviation, and remote-area voice + data comms. Backbone of GMDSS — the Global Maritime Distress and Safety System every ocean-going vessel depends on. Acquired by Viasat in 2023.
